correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the two regression covariances (RESULT.md 48–65): for input K_S x and target Cx they are (r²/2)D I and (r²/2)C E[K_S]^T. The smallest possible D is cos²(θ/2)>0 on 0<θ<π, so the optimizer over all matrices is unique. Subtracting its explained energy from 2r²(1−cos θ)/h² leaves 4r²v(1−cos θ)²/(h²D). This gives the stated exact residual and radial sign, including all deterministic laws. At fixed h the angular derivative of h times the fitted frequency has numerator (1−2q)cos θ+2q and positive denominator D², giving the unique fold or the increasing deterministic-midpoint endpoint case. For a fixed offset law and fixed true ω>0, the radial coefficient starts with (μ−1/2)ω²h; the angular h² and h⁴ coefficients are (q−1/6)ω³ and (q²−q/4+1/120)ω⁵. Thus the full-matrix order criterion, −1/180 coefficient, residual expansion and 2π/3 fold follow. Read VERIFICATION.md and the finite checker without executing it; the checked analytic proof suffices. The fold refers only to the fitted angular coefficient, not identification from all data.

value.rationale: The motivated question is how to choose collocation offsets to recover conservative oscillatory dynamics, not how to maximize a known trigonometric symbol. Deterministic midpoint gives zero risk and no fold but only second-order frequency accuracy; fourth order fixes the variance, gives nonzero irreducible loss and forces a fold within the sampling range. This separates three practically different targets by exact, usable population conditions. The interpretation is limited to the specified noiseless linear model and the angular statistic.
